description: Nigerian Air Force light utility aircraft in the open-air gallery of the National War Museum. Type and serial from the aviationmuseum.eu site page and blog entry, which carry photographs but were last updated 6 December 2016. Site-level presence confirmed for 2022 by a first-hand visitor account and for 2025 and 2026 by a dated visitor guide, both of which describe aircraft in the outdoor gallery, but this individual airframe has not been re-confirmed since 2016.

Nigerian Air Force twin-engine light transport in the museum's open-air gallery. Type and serial from aviationmuseum.eu, last updated 6 December 2016, with the same site-level presence evidence and the same individual-airframe caveat as the other Umuahia entries.

Nigerian Air Force jet bomber of the Civil War period and the single most prominent airframe in the museum's outdoor gallery, appearing in the site's own lead photograph on aviationmuseum.eu. Type and serial from that source, last updated 6 December 2016, with site-level presence confirmed in 2022 and 2025 but no individual re-confirmation.

Fuselage only. One of the Swedish-built light aircraft flown by Biafra as the improvised Biafran Babies strike force during the Nigerian Civil War. aviationmuseum.eu records the marking as BB 905, but the Biafran aircraft carried informal markings rather than national military serials and no independent confirmation was found, so tail_number is left blank and the marking is carried as an alias only. Type and marking from aviationmuseum.eu, last updated 6 December 2016.

Nigerian Air Force fighter in the museum's open-air gallery. Type and serial from aviationmuseum.eu, last updated 6 December 2016. Site-level presence confirmed 2022 and 2025 as with the other Umuahia airframes; this individual aircraft has not been re-confirmed by a dated photograph since 2016.
